'''Kamonaraita Shrine''' (かもならいたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kanan, Osaka|Q2305508|qid=Q2305508}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|Q1347323|qid=Q1347323}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} system it was a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The principal enshrined deities are Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto, Amasu Teru Chiteru Hikohomino-Mikoto, and Kushitama-no-Mikoto, but all are alternate names of {{ill|Nigihayahi|Q10949054|qid=Q10949054}}. Because this area was within the sphere of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|Q1755836|qid=Q1755836}}, this is considered a shrine that took the Mononobe ancestral deity Nigihayahi as its main deity. However, because the shrine name contains "Kamo," there is also a theory that the original deity was related to the {{ill|Kamo clan|Q122979436|qid=Q122979436}}.

In the auxiliary sanctuary, {{ill|Takamimusubi|UNKNOWN|Takamimusubi|lt=Taka-mi-musubi no Mikoto}} is enshrined.

=== History ===
Its founding background is unknown, but it is thought to date from before Engi 7. It is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} as "Kamonaraita Shrine, Ishikawa District, Kawachi Province" and classified as a minor shrine, but it later declined and its location became unknown.

The present Kamonaraita Shrine was a shrine that, until the Meiji period, was called "Tenmangū" and enshrined {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}}. In November {{ill|1660|Q7001|qid=Q7001}} (Manji 3), because the shrine building of nearby Tenjin Kamiyama Shrine, which enshrined Taka-mi-musubi no Mikoto, was destroyed by a storm, it was merged into this shrine. It was identified as the Shikinai Kamonaraita Shrine, renamed to its present shrine name, and the principal deity was changed to Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto. In Meiji 5, it was ranked as a village shrine.
